title: Drupal Core Lab accessibility scenario (lab-a11y-scenario/1)
description: A small data-only description of one accessibility checkpoint flow: an initial route, an ordered list of steps, the named checkpoints to capture, and the assertions to record. It is replayed against Before and After by tools/playwright/scenario-run.mjs. There is no scripting language: custom JavaScript is limited to one bounded, read-only `evaluate` expression per step, and validation refuses anything that can click, focus, type, navigate, reload, submit or write storage. Locators are semantic; an MCP element reference such as `e12` is rejected because those are session-scoped.

id.description: Stable lower-case identifier. Kept stable so evidence and comparisons can be tied to it.

issue.description: drupal.org issue number, or null when there is no issue yet.

variant.description: Registered variant slug that provides the Before/After patch stacks, or null when no environment is registered yet. The runner refuses an unregistered variant instead of writing a fake result; the scenario does not duplicate patch stacks.

description.description: What the flow reaches and why those states matter. Behaviour specific to this issue; do not copy another scenario's expectations.

preconditions.description: What must be true before the scenario can run (fixture, modules, theme, environment).

recipe.description: Recipe path or name that creates the starting state.

standardInstall.description: True for a plain Standard install with no recipe. Never set together with recipe.

notes.description: What the fixture provides and what it does not. Say where the fixture path exists in this checkout.

route.description: Initial path. The goto step repeats it; this field is what the report shows as the starting state.

login.description: Whether each side is logged in with the lab's one-time link before the scenario starts (openSide does this).

browser.description: Browser engine. A checkpoint's environment records what actually launched; nothing is extrapolated to another engine.

colourScheme.description: prefers-color-scheme emulation. Default Admin's dark mode is a class applied when this is dark and the theme is set to auto.

forcedColors.description: Emulate prefers-forced-colors: active. This is emulation, not a real Windows contrast theme; say so in limits.

steps.description: Ordered steps. Waits are explicit readiness conditions; there is no sleep action.

label.description: Human label for the report. A step without a label is described by its action.

optional.description: Only for genuinely optional UI: a locator that cannot be found is recorded as skipped, not failed. Never use it to hide a required step.

key.description: press: a Playwright key name such as Tab, Enter, Escape, ArrowLeft or Shift. Shift on a locator is a documented way to place trusted keyboard focus on an element without activating it.

value.description: fill/selectOption: the value to enter or select.

id.description: checkpoint: id of a declared checkpoint to capture.

expression.description: evaluate: ONE bounded read-only in-page expression (for example getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('.ck-editor__editable')).backgroundColor). It must not change state: no click, focus, typing, navigation, reload, submit, storage or DOM writes. This is not an unrestricted host-code endpoint.

checkpoints.description: Named application states. A step {action:'checkpoint', id} captures the matching entry. Every declared checkpoint must be captured.

profile.description: Engine/collector profile used at this checkpoint (default quick). Use visual where computed styles or screenshots matter and dynamic where announcements matter.

scope.description: CSS selector of the element this checkpoint is about. Used for the visual evidence; not a substitute for a semantic locator in click/fill steps.

tags.description: WCAG tags passed to the engines, for example wcag22aa.

rules.description: Engine rule ids to limit or require, for example color-contrast.

expected.description: Facts BOTH sides must share at this state. State-dependent checkpoints need this so the comparison refuses a difference between non-equivalent states. Do not put focus here when focus is the behaviour under test; use a per-side assert instead.
Scenario-level assertions, evaluated on each side after the last step. A failure on After is unexpected; a Before failure with an After pass is the change under test.

regressionAssertions.description: Behaviour that must not get worse. Also evaluated per side; a Before pass with an After failure is a regression.

resetInstructions.description: How a person resets the fixture (database snapshot, environment reset) before replaying.

manualReview.description: Checks the replay cannot make: what a person must do (keyboard pass, real screen reader, real Windows contrast theme, contrast measurement by eye). Stored separately from automated results.

limits.description: What this scenario does not cover, including anything inferred rather than observed.

verified.description: True only after the scenario reached every checkpoint against a real Before/After pair and a person read the result. Everything in this repository starts false.

notes.description: Which lab files were read, which steps were inferred from the issue or report, which fixture paths exist, and what is missing.

locator.description: A semantic locator. Exactly one kind is used. The selector is a last resort for markup with no usable role/label/text/testId handle (for example <summary>, which Playwright does not map to a role); say why in the scenario notes. An MCP element reference such as e12 is rejected.

role.description: ARIA role, for example option, button, link, checkbox, textbox.

name.description: Accessible name (case-insensitive substring by default; set exact:true for an exact match). Required with role.

readiness.description: An explicit state to wait for. Fixed sleeps are never accepted.

expression.description: Boolean expression evaluated in the page (for example !!document.querySelector('.ck-editor__editable')).

stateExpectation.description: A dotted path into a checkpoint record (for example state.application.messages or focus.active.role) with one comparison.

equivalence.description: Facts two sides must share before their findings or assertions are compared. equivalence() refuses a comparison when one of these fails.

content.description: Text that must be visible on both sides.

check.description: One data-only assertion. Exactly one check type per object; each records pass/fail with the evidence it looked at.

within.description: CSS selector the focused element must be inside. Use it for 'focus returned to the editor' without pretending to know the exact toolbar button.

via.description: announce: Drupal.announce() call; live: text change inside a live region (role alert/status/log or aria-live).

silentChange.description: True: at least one observed text change had no announcement, live region, focus move or disclosure; false: none did. What a screen reader would actually say is still a manual check.

equivalence.description: Decided by compareScenario() against the paired Before/After records, not on one side.
